info.description: Identify visitors, read identification events and manage your integration. Every request is authenticated with a key in the `x-api-key` header. Guides and field-by-field reference: https://docs.fingerly.io
info.title: Fingerly API

post.description: Issues a one-time, five-minute challenge bound to the authenticated key. Android has the device keystore attest to it and iOS signs it with App Attest; either way the evidence goes in the identify request, and a report that does not carry one of these challenges is never treated as proven.

post.description: Marks one identification event as consumed, atomically and once per organization, so a request ID handed from a page to your backend backs one decision only. The first call answers `200` with `first: true`; every later call answers `409 event_already_consumed`, with the first consume's time in the error's `details` entry for the field `consumed_at`. Read and check the event before you consume it. The flag is kept with the event and erased with it.

put.description: Spends the write DeviceCheck token held for this iOS event, once, to set bit0, bit1 or both with Apple, using your project's own Apple key. A bit left out keeps its value. The bits mean what you decide; Fingerly never reads them. Apple answers a write with no previous value; the event's read token, spent by the query route, is separate, so one identification supports one read and one write. Tokens are held for one hour, only for events whose App Attest evidence covered them, and only when DeviceCheck is switched on for the project's Apple credential. After a `503`, retry with the same bits: a token kept for a retry accepts only the request it was first used for.

bit1.description: The value to set for the second bit. Leave out to keep it

Apple asks for each token to be used once, so the event holds a second token for the write route: to read and then mark a device, read and write on the same identification. After a `503`, retry the read: a token kept for a retry accepts only the request it was first used for.

post.description:
Submits the signal report a client SDK collected and answers with the request ID, the visitor ID and its confidence. There is no second call to make.

A browser, an app, a proxy and a hosted domain also receive `suspect_score` and `suspect_level`, unless the key withholds them, and never `triggers`. A secret key called directly from a backend receives the score, the level and the `triggers`.

The client SDKs build and send this request. `signals` is produced by them and is not a public contract. Send an `Idempotency-Key` header, and the same value on every retry, so a retried identification is answered and charged once.

The `X-Request-Id` response header names this HTTP exchange, for support and logs. It is not the `request_id` in the body, which names the identification and is what `GET /events/{request_id}` reads.

409.description: The Idempotency-Key was reused with a different payload, or the original request is still in progress

429.description: The SDK key or the organization is over its rate limit; retry after Retry-After. A secret key called from a backend is also told which limit in Fingerly-RateLimit-Scope

post.description:
The one URL the client SDKs and every first-party proxy post to. Forwards the single-pass v3 identification envelope and answers `200` with the verdict, exactly as the identify route answers.

It exists so a proxy can forward everything it receives to a single path of the customer's choosing, with nothing appended that a content blocker could match across sites. An `Idempotency-Key` header is required on every call.

The `X-Request-Id` response header names this HTTP exchange, for support and logs. It is not the `request_id` in the body, which names the identification and is what `GET /events/{request_id}` reads.

post.description:
Owner or admin, or an admin management key. Archives the project if it is not archived yet - its keys are revoked at once, so no new data arrives - and deletes all of its data: its archived submissions, its stored identifications and rollups, its visitor identities, the webhook events that name it, its keys' attestation state and its Apple and Google platform credentials. There is no undo.

It runs twice: ten minutes after the request, and again a day after the first pass finished, for anything delivered late. Asking while a pass is pending returns it; asking after the purge finished queues another pass. Usage counts and the project's revoked keys are kept, because invoices and usage reports name them.

`archive_copies_expire_by` is when the last archived copy written before per-project archiving expires.

delete.description:
Erases everything this platform holds about one visitor. The identity goes at once, with the webhook events that name the visitor, so a device that comes back is a new visitor from that moment. The stored identifications, their deferred reports and the archived submissions follow within the hour, and the erasure's status turns from `pending` to `done`.

Asking again while one is pending returns that one. An identifier this organization never saw is accepted and erases nothing. Counts already folded into the dashboards are kept: they hold no identifier. Backups age out on their own thirty-day schedule.
